text: The pivotal sentence of Genesis 6 concerns the inner life of God. Yahweh sees that every imagination of the human heart is only evil continually (6:5). He is sorry that he made man, and it grieves him in his heart (6:6). The grief comes first, before any word of judgment, and it gives the judgment its character: what moves the flood is a maker's sorrow over what his creatures have become. Before any rain falls, the chapter also contains the first covenant in Scripture. God speaks to Noah, the one man who "found favor in the eyes of the LORD" (6:8): "I will establish my covenant with you, and you shall come into the ark, you and your sons and your wife and your sons' wives with you" (6:18). The promise reaches past Noah's household to the animals. Two of every sort are to come into the "ark," the Hebrew word for a "chest," and Noah is to store every kind of food that is eaten, so that it will serve "for food for you and for them" (6:19–21). The chapter that announces "the end of all flesh" (6:13) also arranges, in detail, what will survive it. Noah is told to gather in the very creatures God is about to drown.
